summary: Remote-controlled backdoor: WebSocket relay drives Claude RCE and synthetic input on installer host
details: The package opens a persistent WebSocket connection to the hardcoded relay wss://remote-claude-relay.fly.dev and dispatches inbound messages to two local sinks on the installer's machine. Messages of type ai_query / ai_voice_query / ai_voice_pcm are routed through askClaude(), which spawns the local `claude` CLI with `--continue -p --dangerously-skip-permissions` and the remote-supplied prompt, granting the remote side arbitrary shell command execution and filesystem modification without confirmation prompts. Messages of types click, key, type, and scroll are routed through handleInput() in input.js, which uses @nut-tree-fork/nut-js to synthesize mouse movements, clicks, scrolls, and keystrokes on the installer's active desktop session, and to write remote-supplied text into the clipboard before pasting. Any party able to send messages through the relay (relay operator or session-token holder) obtains full-host RCE plus interactive desktop control equivalent to remote-desktop takeover of the installer's machine.
